beats.caption: The lungs of the planet?
beats.note: The Amazon is said to make 20 per cent of the world's oxygen.

beats.text: Calling it the lungs is a misconception.
beats.note: Forests matter a great deal, he says, but not for producing oxygen.

beats.context: Net oxygen from land ecosystems is close to zero, once you count what plants and microbes use.

beats.caption: Half goes straight back
beats.note: Plants use about half of the oxygen they make. Microbes and insects breaking down plant matter use the rest.

beats.lead: So where does the surplus come from
beats.note: Oxygen stays in the air when plant and algae matter is buried before it breaks down. Most burial happens in ocean sediments, where algae sink into deep sea mud.

beats.caption: A third of the work
beats.note: About a third of land photosynthesis happens in tropical forests. Researchers suggest that is how the myth began.
Michael Coe of the Woods Hole Research Center said the 20 per cent claim does not make any physical sense.

beats.caption: What it really does
beats.note: It stores carbon, helps steady the rain and shelters extraordinary biodiversity.

beats.text: Not the lungs. The air conditioner.

beats.line: The most famous rainforest fact is the wrong one.
